defects.title: the rolling-window safety guard degrades SILENTLY to no-guard
defects.detail: `try: import window_policy / except Exception: WP_OK=False; window_policy=None`. WP_OK is read at lines 217, 236 and 783 purely as a gate and is NEVER logged, warned, or surfaced. If window_policy.py is missing, unimportable, or raises at import, the entire T628/T677 window-resilience policy (family cooldown, token meter, reset watcher) vanishes and the keeper reports a normal run. This is the T362/T428 'degraded mode nobody can see' class that regression-task-identity.sh:9-11 was written to kill — and that regression is itself orphaned (T678-D5).
defects.would_a_regression_catch_it: NO — regression-window-resilience.sh imports window_policy directly, so it tests the module, never the keeper's fallback branch. A seeded-defect arm (hide the module, assert the keeper says so loudly) does not exist.
defects.fix_row: make the import failure LOUD: print a WARN line and fail the keeper's startup self-check; add the seeded arm

defects.title: nothing gates that a script build.zig invokes is tracked in git
defects.detail: `zig build test` hard-depends on 66 tools/*.sh paths via addSystemCommand. No gate asserts those paths are committed. Evidence from this census window: at census open (2026-08-22T20:16Z) BOTH tools/regression-window-resilience.sh (a test_step dependency, build.zig:734-736) and tools/window_policy.py (imported by the LIVE fleet keeper) were untracked. The T677 console committed them at 735db2b at ~22:1xZ, mid-census. For those hours a fresh clone's suite would have failed on a missing step and the live keeper would have silently run with no window guard (see T678-D1). The condition closed by luck of a concurrent row, not by a mechanism.
defects.would_a_regression_catch_it: NO — no such check exists in tools/hooks/pre-commit, regression-precommit.sh, regression-suite-surfaces.sh or tools/smoke.sh (grep for ls-files across all four: zero hits).
defects.fix_row: a gate that extracts every tools/ path from build.zig's addSystemCommand calls and asserts `git ls-files --error-unmatch` on each; ship it with a seeded-defect control (an untracked referenced script) and a null control

defects.title: the deploy gate provenance-checks 6 of 8 deployed binaries
defects.detail: deploy_check runs for managent, weizigo-claimlint, weizigo-gtp, weizigo-chainability, weizigo-engine-vs-engine, weizigo-reachcensus. `zig build deploy` also deploys bin/weizigo-arena (deploy-arena) and bin/weizigo-oracle (deploy-oracle) — neither is checked. So a stale or wrong-tool arena/oracle passes smoke silently, which is exactly the T268 class smoke.sh exists to close. The arena omission is masking a deeper hole: src/arena.zig has NO version-banner code, so bin/weizigo-arena carries no build stamp at all and `deploy_check weizigo-arena` would FAIL 'missing or unstamped' if added. weizigo-oracle is a second deploy of the gtp binary and reports itself as 'weizigo-gtp', so the wrong-tool negative control cannot distinguish them either.
defects.would_a_regression_catch_it: NO — tools/smoke.sh has ZERO regression coverage of its own: no null control, no seeded-defect control, in violation of orient principle 4 and the never-trust-a-green-test doctrine.
defects.fix_row: add a version banner to src/arena.zig, give weizigo-oracle its own tool name, extend deploy_check to all 8, and ship regression-smoke.sh with a seeded stale binary

defects.title: three tools do real work when asked for --help
defects.detail: tools/gen-indices has no argv handling whatsoever: `tools/gen-indices --help` rewrote three TRACKED docs (docs/INDEX-claim-{evidence,deps,task}.md) during this census — observed, then reverted with `git checkout --`. tools/race-c-prepare.py likewise rewrote 11 race lane inputs and the sealed KEY.json (byte-identical in fact: the script is deterministic over immutable findings files, so no harm done). tools/dispatch_verify.py documents at :1115 that unknown flags are IGNORED, so a typo'd flag runs the gate instead of erroring. Across ~100 executable surfaces exactly TWO honour --help by design (tools/bakeoff.sh, bin/managent -h); the rest of the argparse tools get it for free and 3 tools mutate on it.
defects.would_a_regression_catch_it: NO for all three — gen-indices is mentioned by regression-absorption-machinery only in passing, race-c-prepare.py has zero coverage, and no regression asserts that an unknown flag is refused.
defects.fix_row: a `--help`-is-inert arm across every tool in bin/ and tools/, driven off a manifest so a new tool cannot skip it

defects.title: 4 regression scripts are written, committed, and never run
defects.detail: No addSystemCommand in build.zig and no tracked caller — only untracked notes mention them (untracked/T322-wire-orphaned-controls.md names two of them, so it is a KNOWN and unfixed gap). regression-process-ownership.sh is 47,850 bytes and regression-task-identity.sh is 12,034 bytes of unexecuted gate. The linkage to this row's specimen is direct: regression-task-identity.sh is the DEEPEST `managent liveness` regression in the tree (its arms 1-4 pin never-beat / beats-stopped / beating and a real SIGKILL), and it is one of the four that never runs.
defects.would_a_regression_catch_it: self-referential — this IS the missing coverage. The generalised gate is the same mechanism as T678-D2: reconcile tools/regression-*.sh against build.zig's addSystemCommand set.
defects.fix_row: wire the four (or retire them with an epitaph — ratified, never silent), then add the reconciliation gate

defects.title: 8 managent verbs are dispatched but absent from `managent help`
defects.detail: archive, holds, needs, purge, reopen, set, shape, verdict. Two of these matter operationally: `purge` is DESTRUCTIVE and undocumented, and `reopen` is the documented repair for a wedged row — bin/dispatch's own refusal message tells the operator to run `bin/managent reopen T678`, a verb `managent help` does not mention. 37 verbs are dispatched in main.zig; 29 are in help.
defects.would_a_regression_catch_it: NO — no regression reconciles the dispatch table against the help text, and 7 verbs (assign, holds, needs, shape, sync, whoami, why) have ZERO regression coverage of any kind.
defects.fix_row: a help-completeness arm: every std.mem.eql dispatch arm must appear in the help body

defects.title: `managent help` writes 100% to stderr and prints a literal backslash-n
defects.detail: `bin/managent help 2>/dev/null | wc -c` = 0; all 4,629 bytes go to stderr, so `managent help | grep <verb>` finds nothing while `managent status --json` correctly uses stdout. Separately, main.zig:7173 carries `\\nTest isolation (T427 ...)` inside a Zig multiline string, so the rendered help shows a literal `\n` before 'Test isolation' instead of a blank line.
defects.would_a_regression_catch_it: NO — `$MG help` is invoked by 9 regression scripts, but every one uses it as a liveness ping; none asserts on its stream or its content.
defects.fix_row: send help to stdout (diagnostics stay on stderr); drop the stray escape

defects.title: a bare `managent next` mutates the live kanban and attributes the claim to 'unknown'
defects.detail: OBSERVED DURING THIS CENSUS, and I caused it: `bin/managent next` with no arguments claimed T578 and stamped identifier `unknown/T578`. `next` takes no --agent, requires no confirmation, and writes a non-canonical agent label — 'unknown' is not in canonical_models, so the row now violates the single-source model-label rule that regression-managent-models.sh exists to enforce. `next` also has ZERO direct regression coverage of the bare form. My attempt to repair it with `bin/managent reopen T578` was BLOCKED by this session's permission classifier, so the row is LEFT DIRTY — see the repair note in `notes`.
defects.would_a_regression_catch_it: NO — regression-managent-models.sh validates labels on claim/agent paths; nothing asserts that `next` produces a canonical label or that a bare `next` is refused.
defects.fix_row: require --agent on next (or inherit MANAGENT_TASK_ID's agent), and validate the label against canonical_models on the next path

defects.title: 9 of 70 regression scripts lack the executable bit; 3 tools are Python named .sh
defects.detail: Non-executable: regression-{absorption-machinery,claim-lifecycle,duplicate-dispatch,managent-concurrency,managent-holds,managent-store-pollution,orcha-acceptance,runner-claude-liveness,runner-harness-p95}.sh, plus tools/suite-truth.sh and 5 tools/*.py. Harmless to `zig build test` (build.zig invokes them as `sh <path>`, not directly) but it means `./tools/regression-claim-lifecycle.sh` fails for a human while the suite passes — an inconsistency that will read as 'this script is broken'. Separately, tools/{fleet-keeper,bakeoff,race-p0-verify}.sh all carry python shebangs under a .sh name; 44 of the bash-shebanged regressions are executed by `sh`, which is harmless on this host (macOS /bin/sh is bash-3.2 in POSIX mode) and I found no bash-4-only constructs (declare -A / mapfile / ${x^^}) in any of them, but it is a portability trap on a dash host.
defects.would_a_regression_catch_it: NO — nothing checks file modes or shebang/extension agreement.
defects.fix_row: chmod +x sweep, rename the three python .sh files, and a mode/shebang consistency arm

defects.title: three generated docs were 20 days stale with no regeneration gate
defects.detail: Discovered as a side effect of T678-D4: docs/INDEX-claim-evidence.md's own header read `Date: 2026-08-02 / Source: CLAIMS.md (303 claims)` while the register now holds 231 claims. Regenerating produced 180 insertions against 324 deletions across the three files. tools/gen-indices is invoked by no build step and by no gate — nothing has regenerated them since 2026-08-02. I reverted the regeneration to keep this census read-only.
defects.would_a_regression_catch_it: NO — gen-indices has effectively no coverage (one incidental mention in regression-absorption-machinery.sh).
defects.fix_row: a freshness arm (regenerate into a temp dir, diff against the committed copies, fail on drift) — the same shape as the claimlint floor

specimen_answer.specimen: `managent liveness` returned `error: SyntaxError` on build 5036557-dirty — a verb broke and nothing caught it.
specimen_answer.status_now: FIXED — `bin/managent liveness` and `liveness --stale-min 5` both return a well-formed surface on build c7e4034-dirty (exit 0). All 15 read-only verbs I exercised are healthy.
specimen_answer.why_nothing_caught_it: Four regression scripts exercise liveness, but (a) the deepest of them, regression-task-identity.sh, is one of the four ORPHANS that build.zig never invokes (T678-D5), and (b) all four call it as `$MG liveness 2>/dev/null` against a SYNTHETIC scratch store — stderr discarded — so a parse failure arising from live-store SHAPE is outside every arm. No regression runs any read-only verb against the live kanban.
tools_with_zero_regression_coverage: tools/gen-version.sh (the build stamp everything else trusts)
specimen_answer.generalisation: the census's own finding is that coverage is measured by MENTION, not by ASSERTION. A verb named in a regression is not a verb whose failure is caught: liveness had 4 mentions and zero arms that would have seen the specimen.

notes: Read-only census, race lane (ruling 7c.35) — I did not read the other four lanes' findings and did not divide the work. NO register proposals: claims and new_rows are deliberately empty, so this file carries no absorption debt. Inbox polled 3x, empty each time, no directives to record. TWO SIDE EFFECTS I CAUSED AND MUST DECLARE: (1) `bin/managent next` (run as part of the verb smoke, before I understood it was mutating) CLAIMED T578 and stamped it `unknown/T578`; my repair `bin/managent reopen T578` was BLOCKED by this session's permission classifier, so T578 IS LEFT in_progress WITH A NON-CANONICAL AGENT LABEL and needs `bin/managent reopen T578` from an operator or an unblocked seat. This became defect T678-D8. (2) `tools/gen-indices --help` rewrote docs/INDEX-claim-{evidence,deps,task}.md; I reverted all three with `git checkout --` and verified the tree clean for those paths. `tools/race-c-prepare.py --help` rewrote untracked/race-c/lanes/*.json + untracked/race-grading/race-c/KEY.json; the script is deterministic over immutable findings inputs so the rewrite is byte-identical, and I left it. Both became defect T678-D4. NOT A DEFECT (checked and cleared): tools/smoke.sh printing 6 STALE lines and still exiting 0 is DELIBERATE and documented at tools/smoke.sh:71-74 per T289 — a build.zig-only commit must not redden the suite; only a missing/unstamped/wrong-tool/unverifiable-provenance binary is a FAIL. The 6 currently-stale deployed binaries are a live operational state, not a tool defect. Also cleared: the 44 bash-shebanged regressions run under `sh` in build.zig with no bash-4-only constructs, so they are correct on this host. Ratified-deletion rule honoured: no row says DELETE — the 5 dead one-shots are MERGE-INTO (demote to fixtures under their owning sprint), per duplication-is-the-oracle.
